name: Izhar
overview: Izhar is a male member of the tribe of Levi, distinguished as the son of Kohath according to Exodus 6:18. His identity is primarily defined by this lineage within the Levitical family. There are no additional notes expanding on his personal characteristics or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Izhar means 'the shining one,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with no indication of divine origin. Another associated name, Amminadab, means '[my] people are generous,' though it is not directly linked to Izhar himself but appears in related genealogical records.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Izhar as the son of Kohath (Exodus 6:18). Inferred relationships suggest he was the father of Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri (Exodus 6:21), and an ancestor of Shelomith (1 Chronicles 23:18). These connections place him firmly within the Levitical lineage important for priestly duties.
scriptureSignificance: Izhar's significance lies chiefly in his role within the Levitical genealogy, serving as a link in the priestly line descending from Kohath. This lineage is foundational for understanding the organization and heritage of the Levites, who were set apart for service to God. Though not prominent for individual actions, Izhar's place in the genealogical record underscores the faithfulness of God's covenantal promises through the tribe of Levi.
